name: Question 7
problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u{v}^{2} \\ {u}^{2}+2v\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=u{v}^{2}$ and $y(u,v)={u}^{2}+2v.$ 

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & ={v}^{2} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =2uv \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =2u & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}{v}^{2} & 2uv \\ 2u & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & ={v}^{2}\cdot 2-2uv\cdot 2u \\  & =2{v}^{2}-4{u}^{2}v.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ 2{v}^{2}-4{u}^{2}v & =0 \\ v(2v-4{u}^{2}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $v(2v-4{u}^{2})=0$ defines the line $v=0,$ i.e., the $u$-axis, and the parabola $v=2{u}^{2}$ in the $uv$-plane.

html:
Question 7
?

Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation T, where T is defined as

T:[uv]⟶[uv2u2+2v].

a
The critical points lie on the lines u=−2v and u=v.
b
The critical points lie on the line v=0 and on the parabola v=2u2.
c
The critical points lie on the parabola u=v2.
d
The critical points lie on the line v=0 and on the hyperbola v2−u2.
e
The critical points lie on the line u=2v.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a transformation

T:[uv]→[x(u,v)y(u,v)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y)∂(u,v), is given by

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂y∂u∂y∂v|.

To find the locations of the critical points of T, we need to solve ∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=0.

Here, we have x(u,v)=uv2 and y(u,v)=u2+2v.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂x∂u=v2∂x∂v=2uv∂y∂u=2u∂y∂v=2

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂y∂u∂y∂v|=|v22uv2u2|=v2⋅2−2uv⋅2u=2v2−4u2v.

The function has critical points when ∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=0. So, we obtain

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=02v2−4u2v=0v(2v−4u2)=0.

The equation v(2v−4u2)=0 defines the line v=0, i.e., the u-axis, and the parabola v=2u2 in the uv-plane.
